annotationRationale: Isosceles base angles establish the right angle, and the Pythagorean theorem gives the 3:8 side ratio. Isosceles altitude-midpoint properties and AA similarity transfer that ratio to segments on AB.
sourceMethod: Follows the official isosceles-angle argument, 3-4-5 triangle, and perpendicular projections onto AB. Explicitly defines both perpendicular feet and justifies the midpoint and similarity relations shown in the source.

review.mathCheck: The isosceles base angles and complementary angles at A and B force ∠CDE=90°. Thus CE=5x and BC=8x. The midpoint feet and AA similarity give 3/8=BD/(2BD+AD), hence 3AD=2BD and AD:DB=2:3, choice A. Interior-point assumptions justify the segment sums.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded expansion of official solution 16 across pages 6–7. The auxiliary feet, their midpoint properties and the similarity ratio agree with the official figure, including the order A,F,D,G,B. All constructions are defined in the text.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed isosceles, Pythagorean and similarity nodes match the essential steps. Acute-angle complementarity is appropriately supporting knowledge.
